Date: 2022-06-23 WHAT IS CLAIMED IS:
1. A method for controlling an automated vehicle, wherein the method comprises:
monitoring driving safety information before a vehicle enters a curve or when the vehicle has entered the curve;
obtaining a position of the vehicle in response to the driving safety information;
obtaining curve information, wherein the curve information comprises at least one of a position of a start point of the curve and a position of an end point of the curve; and
controlling, based on the position of the vehicle and the curve information, the vehicle to stop at a position outside the curve.
2. The method according to claim 1, wherein the driving safety information is system fault information; the system fault information indicates that a system fault occurs in the vehicle; and
the monitoring driving safety information comprises:
obtaining the system fault information by detecting a system status of the vehicle.
3. The method according to claim 1, wherein the driving safety information is environmental risk information; the environmental risk information indicates that a driving environment of the vehicle does not meet a risk range preset in an automated driving system; and
the monitoring driving safety information comprises:
obtaining the environmental risk information by detecting a condition of an environment in which the vehicle is located.
4. The method according to claim 1, wherein the driving safety information is curve obstacle information; the curve obstacle information indicates that there is an obstacle blocking traffic in the curve; and
the monitoring driving safety information comprises:
receiving the curve obstacle information sent by a road side unit (RSU).
5. The method according to claim 1, wherein the obtaining curve information comprises:
receiving the curve information sent by a road side unit (RSU).
6. The method according to claim 1, wherein the obtaining curve information comprises:
processing map data in the vehicle to obtain the curve information.
7. The method according to claim 1, wherein the obtaining curve information comprises:
receiving motion trail information sent by a reference vehicle that has entered the curve;
and processing the motion trail information, to obtain the curve information.
8. The method according to claim 1, wherein the controlling, based on the position of the vehicle and the curve information, the vehicle to stop at a position outside the curve comprises:
determining a relative position relationship between the vehicle and the curve based on the position of the vehicle and the curve information, wherein the relative position relationship indicates that the vehicle has not entered the curve or has entered the curve; and
controlling, based on the relative position relationship, the vehicle to stop at the position outside the curve.
9. The method according to claim 8, wherein the controlling, based on the relative position relationship, the vehicle to stop at the position outside the curve comprises:
if the relative position relationship indicates that the vehicle has not entered the curve, controlling the vehicle to stop at a position before the start point of the curve or controlling the vehicle to stop at a position after the end point of the curve; and
controlling, if the relative position relationship indicates that the vehicle has entered the curve, the vehicle to stop at a position after the end point of the curve.
10. The method according to claim 9, wherein the controlling, if the relative position relationship indicates that the vehicle has entered the curve, the vehicle to stop at a position after the end point of the curve comprises:
obtaining a first safety distance, wherein the safety distance is a maximum braking distance for preventing a vehicle behind from colliding with the vehicle; and
controlling the vehicle to stop at a position that is greater than or equal to the first safety distance from the end point of the curve.
11. The method according to claim 10, wherein the curve information further comprises a curvature radius of the curve; and
the obtaining a first safety distance comprises:
obtaining the first safety distance based on the curvature radius of the curve.
12. The method according to claim 11, wherein the obtaining the first safety distance based on the curvature radius of the curve comprises:
performing calculation based on the curvature radius of the curve, to obtain a safety speed of the vehicle; and
obtaining the first safety distance based on the curvature radius of the curve and the safety speed.
13. The method according to claim 11, wherein the obtaining the first safety distance based on the curvature radius of the curve comprises:
searching for mapping information based on the curvature radius of the curve, to obtain the first safety distance, wherein the mapping information comprises a mapping relationship between a combination of a safety speed and the curvature radius and a safety distance.
14. The method according to claim 10, wherein if it is detected that there is a parked vehicle at the position that is greater than or equal to the first safety distance from the end point of the curve, the method further comprises:
obtaining a position of the parked vehicle; and
the controlling the vehicle to stop at a position that is greater than or equal to the first safety distance from the end point of the curve comprises:
obtaining a second safety distance based on the position of the parked vehicle and the first safety distance, wherein the second safety distance is greater than the first safety distance;
and controlling the vehicle to stop at a position that is greater than or equal to the second safety distance from the end point of the curve.
15. The method according to claim 10, wherein if it is detected that there is a parked vehicle at the position that is greater than or equal to the first safety distance from the end point of the curve, the controlling the vehicle to stop at a position that is greater than or equal to the first safety distance from the end point of the curve comprises:
controlling the vehicle to stop at a position in an adjacent lane of a lane in which the parked vehicle that is greater than or equal to the first safety distance from the end point of the curve is located.
16. The method according to claim 1, wherein after the controlling, based on the position of the vehicle and the curve information, the vehicle to stop at a position outside the curve, the method further comprises performing at least one of the following:
indicating the vehicle to turn on hazard warning signal lights to perform danger signal alerting;
indicating the vehicle to start an automatic shutdown instruction to shut down an engine;
indicating a door to be automatically unlocked when the door is locked; and
indicating the vehicle to activate an emergency rescue system.
17. An apparatus for controlling an automated vehicle, comprising at least one processor and at least one memory, wherein the at least one memory is configured to store program instructions, and the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
monitor driving safety information before a vehicle enters a curve or when the vehicle has entered the curve;
obtain a position of the vehicle in response to the driving safety information;
obtain curve information, wherein the curve information comprises at least one of a position of a start point of the curve and a position of an end point of the curve; and
control, based on the position of the vehicle and the curve information, the vehicle to stop at a position outside the curve.
18. The apparatus according to claim 17, wherein the driving safety information is system fault information; the system fault information indicates that a system fault occurs in the vehicle; and
the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
obtain the system fault information by detecting a system status of the vehicle.
19. The apparatus according to claim 17, wherein the driving safety information is environmental risk information; the environmental risk information indicates that a driving environment of the vehicle does not meet a risk range preset in an automated driving system;
and the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
obtain the environmental risk information by detecting a condition of an environment in which the vehicle is located.
20. The apparatus according to claim 17, wherein the driving safety information is curve obstacle information; the curve obstacle information indicates that there is an obstacle blocking traffic in the curve; and
the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
receive the curve obstacle information sent by a road side unit (RSU).
21. The apparatus according to claim 17, wherein the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
receive the curve information sent by a road side unit (RSU).
22. The apparatus according to claim 17, wherein the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
process map data in the vehicle to obtain the curve information.
23. The apparatus according to claim 17, wherein the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
receive motion trail information sent by a reference vehicle that has entered the curve;
and process the motion trail information, to obtain the curve information.
24. The apparatus according to claim 17, wherein the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
determine a relative position relationship between the vehicle and the curve based on the position of the vehicle and the curve information, wherein the relative position relationship indicates that the vehicle has not entered the curve or has entered the curve; and
control, based on the relative position relationship, the vehicle to stop at the position outside the curve.
25. The apparatus according to claim 24, wherein the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
if the relative position relationship indicates that the vehicle has not entered the curve, control the vehicle to stop at a position before the start point of the curve or controlling the vehicle to stop at a position after the end point of the curve; and

26. The apparatus according to claim 25, wherein if the relative position relationship indicates that the vehicle has entered the curve, the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
obtain a first safety distance, wherein the safety distance is a maximum braking distance for preventing a vehicle behind from colliding with the vehicle; and
control the vehicle to stop at a position that is greater than or equal to the first safety distance from the end point of the curve.
27. The apparatus according to claim 26, wherein the curve information further comprises a curvature radius of the curve; and
the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
obtain the first safety distance based on the curvature radius of the curve.
28. The apparatus according to claim 27, wherein the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
perform calculation based on the curvature radius of the curve, to obtain a safety speed of the vehicle; and
obtain the first safety distance based on the curvature radius of the curve and the safety speed.
29. The apparatus according to claim 27, wherein the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
search for mapping information based on the curvature radius of the curve, to obtain the first safety distance, wherein the mapping information comprises a mapping relationship between a combination of a safety speed and the curvature radius and a safety distance.
30. The apparatus according to claim 26, wherein if it is detected that there is a parked vehicle at the position that is greater than or equal to the first safety distance from the end point of the curve, the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
obtain a position of the parked vehicle;
obtain a second safety distance based on the position of the parked vehicle and the first safety distance, wherein the second safety distance is greater than the first safety distance; and
control the vehicle to stop at a position that is greater than or equal to the second safety distance from the end point of the curve.
31. The apparatus according to claim 26, wherein if it is detected that there is a parked vehicle at the position that is greater than or equal to the first safety distance from the end point of the curve, the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
control the vehicle to stop at a position in an adjacent lane of a lane in which the parked vehicle that is greater than or equal to the first safety distance from the end point of the curve is located.
32. The apparatus according to claim 17, wherein the at least one processor is coupled to the at least one memory to execute the instructions to:
indicate the vehicle to turn on hazard warning signal lights to perform danger signal alerting;
indicate the vehicle to start an automatic shutdown instruction to shut down an engine;
indicate a door to be automatically unlocked when the door is locked; and
indicate the vehicle to activate an emergency rescue system.
33. A computer program product comprising computer-executable instructions that are stored on a non-transitory computer-readable medium and that, when executed by at least one processor, cause an apparatus for controlling an automated vehicle to:
monitor driving safety information before a vehicle enters a curve or when the vehicle has entered the curve;
obtain a position of the vehicle in response to the driving safety information obtain curve information, wherein the curve information comprises at least one of a position of a start point of the curve and a position of an end point of the curve; and
control, based on the position of the vehicle and the curve information, the vehicle to stop at a position outside the curve.
34. The computer program product according to claim 33, wherein the driving safety information is system fault information; the system fault information indicates that a system fault occurs in the vehicle; and
when executed by the at least one processor, the computer-executable instructions cause the apparatus to:
obtain the system fault information by detecting a system status of the vehicle.
35. The computer program product according to claim 33, wherein the driving safety information is environmental risk information; the environmental risk information indicates that a driving environment of the vehicle does not meet a risk range preset in an automated driving system; and
when executed by the at least one processor, the computer-executable instructions cause the apparatus to:

36. The computer program product according to claim 33, wherein the driving safety information is curve obstacle information; the curve obstacle information indicates that there is an obstacle blocking traffic in the curve; and

37. The computer program product according to claim 33, wherein when executed by the at least one processor, the computer-executable instructions cause the apparatus to:

38. The computer program product according to claim 33, wherein when executed by the at least one processor, the computer-executable instructions cause the apparatus to:

39. The computer program product according to claim 33, wherein when executed by the at least one processor, the computer-executable instructions cause the apparatus to:

and process the motion trail information, to obtain the curve information.
40. The computer program product according to claim 33, wherein when executed by the at least one processor, the computer-executable instructions cause the apparatus to:
determine a relative position relationship between the vehicle and the curve based on the position of the vehicle and the curve information, wherein the relative position relationship indicates that the vehicle has not entered the curve or has entered the curve; and
control, based on the relative position relationship, the vehicle to stop at the position outside the curve.
